headline_marked: Oil prices surge as [[Iran attacks US base in Jordan]]
headline: Oil prices surge as Iran attacks US base in Jordan
summary: Tehran's missile strikes on the Al-Azraq air base follow US destruction of five Iranian oil tankers, pushing global crude prices toward $100 a barrel.
details: Iran's Revolutionary Guards have launched missile strikes on the US air base of Al-Azraq in Jordan, describing the operation as 'punitive' in retaliation for American strikes on Iranian oil tankers.
The attack targeted maintenance facilities, deployment locations, and fighter jet shelters. Jordan's army reported that it successfully shot down 18 missiles targeting the kingdom.
The escalation follows a US military operation that destroyed five Iranian oil tankers. The US military stated they directed crews to abandon ship before the vessels were hit.
Tensions have peaked as Iran maintains a stranglehold on the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping route for the world's oil and gas, while Washington seeks to choke Iran's economy.
Iran has further warned that oil tankers off the coasts of US-allied Kuwait and Bahrain will be targeted next, urging crews to leave their vessels.
Global oil prices have climbed toward $100 a barrel due to the conflict. Brent crude rose to $99.38, while West Texas Intermediate reached $94.51.
Additional clashes include Iranian claims of attacking two US destroyers with ballistic missiles and the seizure of an American unmanned submarine drone in the Strait of Hormuz.
caption:
Oil prices are hitting $100 a barrel as Iran launches missile strikes on a US base in Jordan.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards have launched missile strikes on the US air base of Al-Azraq in Jordan, describing the operation as 'punitive' in retaliation for American strikes on Iranian oil tankers.

The attack targeted maintenance facilities, deployment locations, and fighter jet shelters. Jordan's army reported that it successfully shot down 18 missiles targeting the kingdom.

The escalation follows a US military operation that destroyed five Iranian oil tankers. The US military stated they directed crews to abandon ship before the vessels were hit.

Tensions have peaked as Iran maintains a stranglehold on the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping route for the world's oil and gas, while Washington seeks to choke Iran's economy.

Iran has further warned that oil tankers off the coasts of US-allied Kuwait and Bahrain will be targeted next, urging crews to leave their vessels.

Global oil prices have climbed toward $100 a barrel due to the conflict. Brent crude rose to $99.38, while West Texas Intermediate reached $94.51.

Additional clashes include Iranian claims of attacking two US destroyers with ballistic missiles and the seizure of an American unmanned submarine drone in the Strait of Hormuz.

headline: 8-hour gas supply suspension in parts of Dhaka this Thursday
summary: Titas Gas will halt supply to several areas including Basabo and Malibagh from 1 PM to 9 PM for maintenance and pipeline relocation work.
details: Titas Gas has announced an 8-hour gas supply suspension for several areas of the capital on Thursday, September 10.
The suspension will be in effect from 1:00 PM to 9:00 PM, affecting both residential and commercial customers.
Impacted areas include Basabo, Khilgaon, Madartek, Shahjahanpur, Sipahibagh, Tilpa Para, Malibagh, Shantibagh, and the Taltala Market area.
The outage is necessary for the installation of walls along the railway line at the Shahjahanpur rail crossing and the relocation of distribution lines for the Dhaka Elevated Expressway project.
Titas Gas authorities have warned that surrounding areas may also experience low gas pressure during this period.
The authority has expressed regret for the temporary inconvenience caused to the customers.
caption:
Gas supply will be off for 8 hours in several Dhaka areas this Thursday.

Titas Gas has announced an 8-hour gas supply suspension for several areas of the capital on Thursday, September 10.

The suspension will be in effect from 1:00 PM to 9:00 PM, affecting both residential and commercial customers.

Impacted areas include Basabo, Khilgaon, Madartek, Shahjahanpur, Sipahibagh, Tilpa Para, Malibagh, Shantibagh, and the Taltala Market area.

The outage is necessary for the installation of walls along the railway line at the Shahjahanpur rail crossing and the relocation of distribution lines for the Dhaka Elevated Expressway project.

Titas Gas authorities have warned that surrounding areas may also experience low gas pressure during this period.

The authority has expressed regret for the temporary inconvenience caused to the customers.
